metadata.scope: final finite-versus-asymptotic explanatory synthesis; no new analytic theorem

question: Why do accessible primitive canonical exactly-one directional counts look close to 2:1:1 although the proved limit is the chamber vector?

finite_lock_B100000.interpretation: the near-2:1:1 shape is already present before the exactly-one sieve; overlap removal is a small finite perturbation

mechanism_ledger.archimedean_backbone: canonical size-order chamber times one-face Gelfand-Leray density; I_ab>I_ac>I_bc
mechanism_ledger.finite_ab_flattening: supported-shell richness is the dominant diagnosed finite mechanism depressing the geometric ab advantage
mechanism_ledger.finite_ac_bc_structure: opposite-signed OE/EE and pure-G contributions cancel strongly; primitive support supplies much of the residual positive ac-bc tilt
mechanism_ledger.overlap_role: finite-small and asymptotically lower order; does not determine the leading normalized vector
mechanism_ledger.asymptotic_arithmetic_role: surviving leading arithmetic population factor is common across directions, so it cancels after normalization
mechanism_ledger.resolution: finite near-2:1:1 is a long pre-asymptotic flattening of the stronger chamber bias

perfect_cuboid_scope.note: lower-order does not imply empty; perfect-cuboid existence remains outside the completed Stage13 claim
